newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadians less optimistic about finances - survey.
newsitem.headline: Canadians less optimistic about finances - survey.

text.p: Canadians are less optimistic than last year that their personal financial situations will improve in the year ahead, according to an Angus Reid Group survey released on Thursday.

The survey, sponsored by accounting firm Ernst & Young, found 27 percent of Canadians anticipate an improved personal financial situation on 1997 over 1996, down eight percent from a similar survey done last year.

This year's survey found 48 percent of Canadians expect their financial situation to remain the same, an increase of five percentage points over last year's poll. The number of Canadians expecting their financial situation to worsen in the next year rose to 24 percent from 21 percent in 1996.

"The modest improvement in the job market last year has disappointed many, leaving unfulfilled expectations. But the increased pessimism could prove well overdone, as 1997 promises the best job and wage growth in three years," said Stephen Tanny, a retail analyst with Ernst & Young, in a statement.

The survey found residents of Ontario and British Columbia are the most optimistic about their prospects. The most optimistic Canadians also tended to be male, between the ages of 18 and 34, university graduates and Canadians with an annual income greater than C$60,000.
The survey also found that paying off or reducing debt will be priority for almost two thirds of Canadians. Half of those surveyed said they plan to save more money in 1996 than 1997.
